note: Authored. A profile lists the classification schemes of one jurisdiction. Each limit of a listed scheme takes its citation, version and check date from that scheme's own source record (the retrieval date is the check date). review_by is the authored date after which the profile blocks verdicts until it is re-checked and re-dated.

profiles.name: United States, NRC
profiles.framework: Near-surface disposal classification, 10 CFR 61.55. Fusion machines would be licensed under the byproduct material framework (10 CFR Part 30) proposed by the NRC on 2026-02-26.
profiles.framework_status: 10 CFR 61.55 is in force. The Part 30 fusion-machine framework is a proposed rule: 'Regulatory Framework for Fusion Machines', proposed rule, document 2026-03865, published 2026-02-26, comments closed 2026-05-27. A Federal Register API search of NRC documents on 'fusion machines' on 2026-10-16 found no later document for it, so no final rule was found.

framework_citations.title: Regulatory Framework for Fusion Machines (proposed rule)

profiles.review_note: Three months, because a final fusion-machine rule may change the framework.

profiles.name: United Kingdom
profiles.framework: UK solid LLW definitions (LLW, VLLW) from the UK LLW strategy and policy, and the England and Wales out-of-scope concentrations of the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 Schedule 23.
profiles.framework_status: The definitions are those of the February 2016 UK strategy, which repeats the 2007 policy wording. Energy Act 2023 section 156 (fusion energy facilities: nuclear site licence not required) was read on legislation.gov.uk on 2026-10-16. Schedule 23 values apply in England and Wales only; Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own regulations, which FARIS does not carry.

profiles.name: International Atomic Energy Agency
profiles.framework: Clearance levels of IAEA GSR Part 3 Schedule I Table I.2 and the summation rule of paragraph I.14.
profiles.framework_status: GSR Part 3 (STI/PUB/1578, 2014) is the standard whose table is encoded. The requirement basis also names GSG-18 (2023) for clearance; FARIS has not transcribed GSG-18 values.

profiles.name: Literature limits, Fetter, Cheng and Mann (1990)
profiles.framework: Specific-activity limits for Class C shallow-land burial of activated metal from the peer-reviewed literature. Not a regulation of any jurisdiction.
profiles.framework_status: A 1990 journal article built on the 10 CFR 61 intruder model; it is not updated and carries no legal force. It is kept in its own profile so that it is never read as an NRC limit.
